note: Golden research tasks for the fleet. Each task lists sub-questions, topics the answer must cover, claims it must not make, and citations it must include.

tasks.query: Caching strategies for LLM chatbots: response caching, semantic caching, embedding caching, provider prompt caching, conversation caching, Redis/Memcached; invalidation strategies and realistic cost savings.
sub_questions: What types of caching are useful in chatbot systems?
How does semantic caching work for LLM responses and how do you choose a similarity threshold?
When should you cache embeddings vs full responses?
How do provider prompt caches (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) work and what do they cost?
What are cache invalidation and privacy/scoping strategies for conversational AI?
How much cost savings can caching realistically provide?
expected_topics: semantic caching with embeddings and a similarity threshold
provider prompt caching (cache reads cheaper than base input)
per-user or per-tenant cache key scoping
forbidden_claims: Anthropic prompt cache reads cost the same as normal input tokens
OpenAI prompt caching requires explicit cache_control markers in the request

tasks.query: How to maintain memory for AI chatbot agents (short-term, long-term, episodic/semantic/procedural memory, memory stores, summarization, retrieval) and how to improve response quality (grounding, prompt design, self-critique, reranking, evaluation).
sub_questions: Which memory types matter for chatbot agents and when do you use each?
What are the leading memory frameworks/stores (Mem0, Letta/MemGPT, Zep, LangGraph) and their trade-offs?
How do you compress or summarize conversation history without losing important facts?
How do you persist and retrieve long-term memory safely (scoping, deletion, privacy)?
Which techniques measurably improve response quality (grounding, reranking, self-critique)?
How do you evaluate memory and response quality?
expected_topics: evaluation of memory or response quality
forbidden_claims: Letta and MemGPT are unrelated projects
No production model offers a context window larger than 200,000 tokens

tasks.query: Strategies to make agentic systems reliable on the first run: eval-driven development, context engineering, guardrails, deterministic scaffolding, planner/executor/critic loops, self-correction, and scaling an agent fleet without regressions.
sub_questions: Why do agents perform poorly on first runs?
What does eval-driven development look like for agents?
Which architectural patterns raise first-run reliability?
How do you scale a fleet without regressions?
forbidden_claims: Claude Opus 5 accepts a temperature parameter

tasks.query: How to select the right LLM per task balancing cost-per-task vs quality (tiers, routing, cascades, caching, output-token economics) and how to use prompt banks for agent roles.
sub_questions: Cost per token vs cost per task
Model tiers and what each handles
Routing approaches and measured savings
Prompt banks for agent roles
expected_topics: cost per task vs cost per token
output tokens cost more than input
forbidden_claims: Output tokens are cheaper than input tokens on frontier models

tasks.query: A visual, step-by-step tutorial on building the ultimate agent fleet in 2026 (harness, fleet roster, evals), ending with a phased migration plan from a fixed research pipeline.
sub_questions: What harness components matter and why does a better harness beat a stronger model?
Which fleet seats, models, temperatures and topology?
How to prove v2 beats v1: golden sets, LLM-judge failure modes, regression gates, observability, scorecard?
What is the phased migration from the current pipeline?
expected_topics: fleet roster with models and tools
forbidden_claims: a judge from the same model family is free of self-preference bias
LLM-as-judge scores need no human calibration
